params.name: d2lo
params.let: 0 - c if w == 0 else q - c

params.name: d2hi
params.let: q + c if w == 0 else c

stem: Which of the following is the range of $y = {=a}\operatorname{{=fn}}\theta {=signed(q)}$?
solution: The sine and the cosine of any angle lie between $-1$ and $1$: $-1 \le \operatorname{{=fn}}\theta \le 1$.
Multiply every part by ${=a}$. A negative multiplier reverses the inequality signs, and the ends $-1$ and $1$ become ${=c}$ and $-{=c}$, so $-{=c} \le {=a}\operatorname{{=fn}}\theta \le {=c}$.
Now add the constant ${=q}$ to every part. The lowest value of $y$ is ${=q} - {=c} = {=lo}$ and the highest value of $y$ is ${=q} + {=c} = {=hi}$.

So the range is ${=lo} \le y \le {=hi}$. The negative sign of $a$ changes which value of $\operatorname{{=fn}}\theta$ gives the lowest $y$, but the range is still ${=c}$ below and ${=c}$ above ${=q}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Lets the negative sign of a flip q as well
proposed_misconceptions.description: For an equation such as $y=-3\sin\theta+2$ the student reads the minus sign as applying to the whole right-hand side, so finds the range of $-(3\sin\theta+2)$ instead. The range is mirrored about 0 and the sign of $q$ is reversed, giving $-q-|a|\le y\le -q+|a|$.

notes: Advanced tier: the twist the book's method uses for a < 0 (the range is q+a <= y <= q-a, i.e. q-|a| <= y <= q+|a|). a = -c with c from 2 to 6; q is a non-zero whole number with |q| < 2c, |q| <= 6 and q != c, which guarantees that all five options are different and each is a proper interval (lower end below upper end) for both values of the option switch w. Distractors: ignores q (-c to c); q added at one end only (w picks which end: -c to q+c, or q-c to c); the sine/cosine-from-0-to-1 error carried over to a negative a (a times [0,1] plus q gives q-c to q, so the range ends at q instead of starting there; same catalogued id); and the new negative-sign-flips-q error (range of -(c sin + q)). mc:...:ends-are-the-equation-numbers is not used here (only four distractors are needed). Option texts carry $...$ as the stem does. The stem holds a, q and the function, so instances differ without distinct_by_choices. About 90 distinct instances. As in the standard family, the book's printed options say theta where y is meant; this family says y.
